rationale:
Evidence: the best raced design is iteration 8, which was re-run unchanged in iteration 9 and scored 323.64. It uses sensor span x = ±0.05, kd 0.6, kp 4.0, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.5, sensor_size 0.012, weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2) and last_direction. Oval finishes were 14 of 20, mean oval progress 0.93, and oval steering_oscillation 0.40. Line losses fell on the s-bend (1.00 to 0.75) and held at 1.00 on the slalom.

Change: none. This candidate restores the proven design exactly, as the Evaluator requested, so this iteration races a measured 323.64 baseline rather than an untested variant. kd is not raised above 0.6, since kd gains are shrinking. Speed (base_speed 1.3), sensor_size 0.016 and the ±0.06 span were each measured to lower the score or cut finishes, so they stay closed.

Expected result: about 323, with oval finishes near 14 of 20. Hypotheses: (a) the oval steering_oscillation rise to 0.40 comes from the wider span steering harder at kd 0.6; (b) kd 0.55 at span 0.05 may cut that oscillation without losing finishes. Measurements wanted: per-track line_loss_events, max_error and steering_oscillation, plus oval completion and completion_time, so the next iteration can decide between the kd 0.55 test and a span of about 0.045 at kd 0.6.
